claims.text: Introducing oxide dispersion strengthening improves the high-temperature mechanical capability of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Oxide dispersion strengthening can provide the improvement while limiting alloy density.
Oxide dispersion strengthening can preserve room-temperature mechanical performance.
Powder metallurgy or mechanical alloying can introduce oxide dispersion strengthening into refractory high-entropy alloys.
The intervention will produce oxide particles 10–50 nm in size at a particle volume fraction of 0.01–0.05.
Dispersed oxide particles create obstacles to dislocation movement.
The oxide-particle obstacles reduce dislocation mobility and thereby enhance high-temperature strength.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will improve high-temperature yield strength by 10–20% relative to the same type of alloy without oxide dispersion strengthening.
Oxide dispersion strengthening will improve high-temperature ductility by 5–10% relative to the alloy without oxide dispersion strengthening.
The predicted improvements will hold under tensile loading at 800–1000°C.
